headline: Warm, dry Friday, then a weak, light rain system Saturday and cooler weather.
summary: High pressure is keeping western Washington dry and warm through Friday, with highs in the mid to upper 70s. Breezy easterly winds tonight in the mountains and foothills ease by Friday morning, and fog should be limited. Winds turn back off the ocean Friday afternoon, and a weak front brings light rain Saturday. The lowlands should get very little, the Cascades somewhat more, and central Puget Sound possibly even less. Sunday looks cool and mostly dry. A low-pressure system may bring rain early next week, but most computer models keep it south of the area, so the detailed forecast favors dry, cool weather Monday. Another weak front may bring isolated showers Wednesday into Thursday.
